name: Kang-Petrov Arms KP-22 'Widebody'
description:
The KP-22 is Kang-Petrov's high-capacity duty pistol, a double-stack 10mm Combat Auto variant of the KP frame family that sacrifices concealability entirely in exchange for firepower and round count. The wider grip houses a 22-round magazine, and the heavier slide adds enough mass to tame the 10mm's notoriously snappy recoil—Kang-Petrov's engineers describe it as 'neutral-cycling,' meaning the muzzle returns to point of aim with minimal conscious effort from a trained shooter. The frame is reinforced polymer over a stainless insert at the frame rails, rated for 50,000 rounds before inspection. It ships with Kang-Petrov's modular rail system, a rarity on this tier of gun, allowing aftermarket lights and foregrip adapters to mount without gunsmithing.

The KP-22 is the pistol that mid-tier security operators argue about endlessly. It's too big to conceal comfortably, too heavy for casual carry, and priced at a point that stretches Tier 2 budgets—but the 10mm chambering and 22-round capacity make it a serious tool for anyone who expects to face more than one problem at once. Arcturus Civil Security uses it as an optional upgrade to their standard-issue KP-17 for personnel assigned to high-risk districts. Private security firms working Slagworks contracts buy it in quantity. It's the pistol that says you've thought about what might happen and decided to be ready for the worst version.

On the street, the KP-22 has a reputation for being 'too much gun.' The 10mm round overpenetrates in residential construction, and more than one negligent discharge through a partition wall has been linked to a Widebody in untrained hands. Kang-Petrov's response to this criticism has been, consistently and without apology, to note that the gun comes with a manual safety and a 22-round magazine and that neither of those things are responsible for what you point it at.
specifications:
caliber: 10mm Combat Auto
effective_range: 60m
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic
magazine_capacity: 22 rounds
weight: 1.02 kg
tactical_use: The KP-22 is a duty-carry and active-security weapon. Operators run it in open-carry rigs on belt or drop-leg, almost never concealed. In a firefight, the 22-round magazine and 10mm energy mean most engagements can be handled without a reload, which is tactically significant in chaotic environments where reloads are fumbled under stress. The modular rail makes weapon-mounted lighting standard practice for night-shift security work. Shooters transitioning from 9mm platforms need dedicated 10mm training to manage the heavier recoil, particularly in rapid-fire strings.
cultural_context: The KP-22 sits at the upper edge of what's considered 'working class hardware' in GLMZ. Carrying one signals that you work security or have reason to expect serious trouble. Corp-tier security officers look down on it as a Slagworks product regardless of its performance. the Gray Zone workers who somehow acquire one tend to be treated differently by Arcturus patrols—more caution, more distance, more paperwork. The gun's size makes it impossible to pretend you're not armed.
known_users: Arcturus Civil Security high-risk district personnel
story_hooks: A KP-22 with a filed serial number turns up in the hands of a the Gray Zone worker who shouldn't be able to afford one—and the ballistic signature matches three Arcturus officers killed in what was ruled an industrial accident last month.

A Slagworks facility manager has quietly purchased 40 KP-22s through a shell vendor and stored them in a locked cabinet on-site. He claims it's for an approved security upgrade. The approval paperwork doesn't exist.
